rationale:
Obligations from `requirements.sdk.outlines.Label`: (1) the enum shape `Named(Vec<String>)` and `Hash(String)`; (2) a named label carries decoded name parts; (3) an anonymous label carries the hexadecimal identity hash; (4) the trait impls Clone, Debug, PartialEq and Eq.

- Decoded name parts: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` parses `impl[Thing/Trait%3CT%3E]/...`. It asserts the label equals `Label::Named(vec!["Thing", "Trait<T>"])`. The percent escape is decoded and the parts are split. It also builds `Label::Named(["a/b","c d"])` and checks the re-encoded base.
- Hash label: it parses `use@0123456789AB` and asserts `Label::Hash("0123456789ab")`, so the hash is carried as a hex string. The invalid-hash cases (`use@123`, `zz`, too long) are rejected.
- Enum shape: the test constructs and matches both variants. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` also runs `check_declaration`. That compares the declared enum signature against rustdoc, so the variants and their payload types are enforced.
- Trait impls: `check_declaration` asserts that the rustdoc trait impl set equals the impls listed in the requirement (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq), so a missing or extra impl fails. The parser test also uses `assert_eq!` on labels, which needs PartialEq and Debug. It uses `clone()` on segments, which carry labels.

I found no obligation without a test and no inadequate assertion.

text: A named label carries decoded name parts. An anonymous label carries the hexadecimal identity hash.
